title: Payer allowance for Prescriptions & Renewals retail fills, by financial class
content:
**Revenue cycle payer-class note — Prescriptions & Renewals.**

When a patient moves a Prescriptions & Renewals prescription to a retail pharmacy, the payer allowance follows the financial class recorded on the patient's billing account — the patient's Patient Financial Account — on the day of the move: a Medicaid Managed Care Account allows 34 days; a Medicare Advantage Account or a Medicare Part B Account allows 60 days; a Commercial PPO/POS Account or a Commercial HMO/EPO Account allows 90 days; any other financial class allows the retail standard of 30 days.

| Financial class on the Patient Financial Account | Payer allowance |
|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Account | 34 days |
| Medicare Advantage Account | 60 days |
| Medicare Part B Account | 60 days |
| Commercial PPO/POS Account | 90 days |
| Commercial HMO/EPO Account | 90 days |
| any other financial class | 30 days |

**Points of judgement.**
- The class is the one recorded on the Patient Financial Account, as the account shows it, not the plan the caller describes.
- The two Medicare classes share one figure (60 days), and the two Commercial classes share one figure (90 days).
- The allowance is a figure in whole days; it is read once, on the day the prescription is moved.

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A patient whose Patient Financial Account is a Medicare Part B Account moves a maintenance prescription to a retail pharmacy: the payer allowance is 60 days. Had the account been a Medicaid Managed Care Account on that day, it would have been 34 days.
